unit.title: Perform gas tungsten arc welding process to AWS specification.(Plate)

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: A drawing for a stainless steel plate tank says the seams are to be GTAW welded "to the AWS code the Centre uses". Before any welding starts, what must the team leader find?
options: A GTAW WPS that covers this plate and joint
A price list for argon from two suppliers
A photo of a similar tank made elsewhere
The tank maker's chart of paint colours

questions.stem: The Centre has written its own GTAW procedure for 10 mm carbon steel plate. Under many AWS codes a GTAW procedure is not "prequalified". What must happen before it is used on a job?
options: A trainee reads it aloud to the whole group
The steel supplier signs and stamps the procedure
A test plate is welded, tested and recorded in a PQR
A welder tries it once on the job and looks at it

questions.stem: Andre passed a GTAW groove test on plate welded onto a steel backing strip. Generally, which groove joints does this test cover?
options: Joints with backing, but not open-root joints
Open-root joints only, never joints with backing
Any groove joint, with or without backing
Fillet welds only, in the flat position

questions.stem: Which pair of plate groove tests generally qualifies a GTAW welder for groove welds on plate in all positions?
options: 1G and 2G
3G and 4G
1G and 3G
2F and 4F

questions.stem: Shanice qualified on a 10 mm GTAW plate test. The new job is on 30 mm plate. What should the supervisor check first?
options: That she has her own torch and set of cups
That the plate has been primed on both sides
That the argon cylinder in her bay is full
That 30 mm is inside her qualified thickness range

questions.stem: Why must plate joints for GTAW be cleaned to bright metal more carefully than joints for MMAW?
options: Bright metal makes the arc easier to see
Clean steel reacts with argon and gets stronger
GTAW has no flux to deal with oil, rust or scale
Dirt on the plate would catch fire in the arc

questions.stem: Plate is wiped with acetone before GTAW. Which precaution is right?
options: Keep the open can beside the torch for later
Let it dry fully and keep the rag away from the arc
Wipe it on while the arc is running to save time
Use plenty, so the plate is still wet when welded

questions.stem: Why is ER70S-2 often chosen as the GTAW filler for carbon steel plate?
options: It holds extra deoxidisers that help give sound weld metal
It is the only rod that will melt in an argon arc
It is a stainless rod, so the weld never rusts
It means the plate needs no cleaning at all

questions.stem: A carbon steel bracket plate must be GTAW welded to a 304 stainless steel plate. Which filler is generally used?
options: ER70S-2
ER308L
ER309L

questions.stem: Why are GTAW filler rods stamped or flagged with their class at one end?
options: So the welder knows which end to hold
So the rod melts more evenly in the pool
So the inspector can measure each rod
So rods of different classes are not mixed up

questions.stem: Why do many test rules ban scratch starting on GTAW test plates?
options: It uses far more argon than other starts
It can leave bits of tungsten in the weld
It makes the arc too cold to weld steel
It rubs the mill scale back onto the joint

questions.stem: What is the job of the post-flow gas at the end of a GTAW run?
options: To cool the plate down quickly
To blow loose slag off the weld
To start the next arc more easily
To shield the hot tungsten and crater as they cool

questions.stem: During a 3G plate test, the tungsten dips into the pool. What should the welder do?
options: Stop, regrind the tungsten and grind out the spot
Keep welding, as the tungsten will burn clean
Turn the current up to melt the tungsten away
Add more filler to cover the spot and carry on

questions.stem: Why is a tungsten ground with the grinding marks running along its length, and not round it?
options: It makes the tungsten last much longer
It lets the cup fit more tightly
It gives a steadier arc that stays on the point
It turns a pure tungsten into a ceriated one

questions.stem: In a 2G (horizontal) GTAW groove on plate, where is the filler usually added, to stop the pool sagging?
options: At the lower edge of the pool
At the upper edge of the pool
Behind the pool, on the cooled bead
Into the arc, well above the plate

questions.stem: A trainee wants to weld his 3G GTAW plate test downwards because it is faster. The WPS says upwards. What do you tell him?
options: Weld upwards: the WPS sets the direction
Weld downwards: speed matters most in a test
Weld either way if the cap looks good
Weld the root down and the cap up

questions.stem: In the "lay wire" method for a GTAW root on plate, what does the welder do?
options: Lays the rod flat on the bench to keep it straight
Lays a wire brush on the joint between the passes
Lays a copper wire behind the root as a backing
Lays the rod in the root and melts it in as he moves

questions.stem: On a 4G (overhead) GTAW groove, the pool keeps dropping. Which change helps most?
options: A bigger pool, so it holds in place
A longer arc and a larger cup
A smaller pool: less current, small dabs of rod
More gas flow, to push the pool up

questions.stem: Why does GTAW on aluminium plate burn bare skin so quickly?
options: Argon burns the skin as it leaves the cup
The arc gives strong ultraviolet, and the bright plate reflects it
Aluminium gives off heat that passes through cloth
The filler rod throws hot sparks onto the arms

questions.stem: Argon is heavier than air. Where can it build up when GTAW plate work is done in a shop?
options: Near the roof, under the sheets
In the open yard on a windy day
Only inside the cylinder itself
In pits, tanks and low closed spaces

questions.stem: A GTAW set with a foot pedal is used where the floor gets damp. Which control is right?
options: Keep the pedal and cables dry, on a dry mat or board
Wrap the pedal in a wet cloth so it stays cool
Work barefoot so the pedal is easier to feel
Turn the set to its highest current to dry the floor

questions.stem: For a GTAW fillet weld test on plate, which pair of tests is commonly used?
options: A hardness test and a paint test
A water test and a leak test
A fillet break test and a macro etch
A pull test and an X-ray of the cap

questions.stem: What does a macro etch of a GTAW fillet weld show the inspector?
options: The make-up of the filler rod
The strength of the weld in N/mm²
The welder's speed and current
The leg sizes, root fusion and penetration

questions.stem: An acid etching solution is mixed for macro tests. Which is right?
options: Add the water quickly to the acid, bare-handed
Add the acid slowly to the water, with goggles and gloves
Mix it in a closed room with the fan off
Mix it in a food container that is close to hand

questions.stem: Before bend strips are cut from a plate coupon welded on a backing strip, what happens to the backing?
options: It is removed flush, by machining or grinding
It is left on, so the strip is stronger
It is painted so the inspector can see it
It is heated red hot to soften it

questions.stem: Why are the ends of a GTAW plate test coupon cut off and not used for bend strips?
options: The ends are always the strongest part
The ends are kept to make the next coupon
The starts and stops there are not typical
The code keeps the ends for a paint test

questions.stem: Why are the long edges of a bend strip rounded off a little before it is bent?
options: So the strip fits in the welder's toolbox
So a crack does not start at a sharp edge
So the strip looks neat in the photo
So the strip bends with much less force

questions.stem: When the cap and root of a bend strip are ground flush, which way should the grinding marks run?
options: Across the strip, at right angles
In small circles over the weld
Any way, as it makes no difference
Along the length of the strip

questions.stem: A root bend from a GTAW plate coupon opens a long crack along the edge of the root. What is the most likely fault?
options: Lack of fusion at the root
Too much argon flow
A tungsten that was too sharp
Too much cleaning before welding

questions.stem: On a 2G plate coupon, the cap has rolled over onto the lower plate without fusing to it. What is this fault?
options: Undercut
Porosity
Overlap
Crater crack

questions.stem: Which tool is used to measure the cap height and undercut depth on a plate coupon?
options: A try square
A weld gauge
A centre punch
A flowmeter

questions.stem: During a test, a welder strikes the arc on the plate surface beside the groove. Why do many codes treat this as a fault?
options: It wastes a lot of argon gas
It makes the tungsten grow longer
It makes the plate thinner there
It can leave a hard spot or a small crack

questions.stem: During a qualification test, which values should the witness record from the welder's set-up?
options: The current, polarity, gas and flow, tungsten and filler
Only the welder's name and the date of the test
Only the time at which the test finished
The price of the filler rods and the argon

questions.stem: What is the main difference between a WPS and a WPQ?
options: A WPS is for pipe; a WPQ is for plate
A WPS is written by the welder; a WPQ by the supplier
A WPS says how to weld; a WPQ shows a welder passed
A WPS lists prices; a WPQ lists the times taken

questions.stem: A GTAW WPS for carbon steel plate was qualified on DCEN. The foreman wants to run the job on AC because the set is already on AC. What is right?
options: AC is fine, as the plate is the same
AC is fine if a larger tungsten is fitted
AC is fine for the cap, but not the root
Not without a WPS that covers AC

questions.stem: The store has run out of pure argon and offers argon with 25% CO2 for a GTAW job. What should the team leader do?
options: Use it, as it is cheaper than argon
Refuse it: CO2 attacks the tungsten
Use it at double the usual flow
Use it for the root pass only

questions.stem: A stainless steel plate is GTAW welded with an open root and no gas on the back. What will the back of the root most likely look like?
options: Rough, dark and crusty ("sugared")
Bright and silver all along
Covered in slag, as with MMAW
As smooth as the face of the cap

questions.stem: One test plate is 150 mm × 300 mm × 10 mm. Steel weighs 7 850 kg per m³. About what does the plate weigh?
options: About 0.35 kg
About 1.2 kg
About 3.5 kg
About 35 kg

questions.stem: Five trainees each weld a 3G and a 4G plate coupon. Each coupon gives one face bend and one root bend. How many strips are bent in all?
On a test day, 6 torches each run at 8 L/min for 2.5 hours of arc time. About how much argon is used?
A plate groove needs 3 passes, each 300 mm long. One 900 mm rod fills about 100 mm of pass. About how many rods does one coupon need?
Two trainees ask to swap coupons so the better welder can finish the other's test. As the person running the test, what do you do?
options: Allow it if both trainees agree
Allow it for the cap pass only
Refuse: each coupon is welded only by the welder named on it
Allow it, as long as the result is still written down

questions.stem: A trainee's 4G coupon fails the root bend. What is the most useful next step for you as the lead?
options: Tell him to retest at once, with no practice
Look at the strip with him and plan practice on the cause
Pass him, since the face bend was good
Keep the result from him so he is not upset

questions.stem: Filler rods for a stainless plate job were left loose on a dusty bench overnight. What should the welder do?
options: Use them just as they are
Heat them red with a torch first
Dip them in water to wash them
Wipe them with solvent, or use rods from a sealed tube

questions.stem: Why does the code limit how high a GTAW cap may stand above the plate?
options: A high cap leaves a sharp notch at the toes
A high cap uses up too much argon
A high cap stops the paint drying
A high cap makes the plate thinner

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: Which AWS position code matches the ISO position PC: a groove weld on plate with the weld running level across an upright plate?
What is the name of the GTAW control that lowers the current slowly at the end of a run, so the crater fills?
Name the gas, used on its own, that is the usual GTAW shielding gas for carbon steel plate.
What do the letters WPQ stand for on a welder's test record?
A test coupon is 300 mm long. The root is welded at 75 mm per minute. How many minutes does the root take?
Name the bend test in which the root side of the weld is on the outside of the bend.
What is the name of the small mark left on the plate where the arc was struck outside the joint?
What is the AWS position code for a fillet weld on plate in the horizontal position?
Bend strips 38 mm wide are cut from 200 mm of good weld, allowing 3 mm for each saw cut. How many full strips can be cut?
What is the name of the groove melted into the plate beside the toe of a cap and left unfilled?
Name the measuring tool, with a blade and a scale in degrees, used to check the bevel angle on a plate edge.
A coupon takes 3 passes of 6 minutes each, with 2 minutes of cleaning between passes. How many minutes is that in all?
What is the name of the first pass laid at the bottom of a groove, which fuses the two plates together?
For this test, the cap may stand no more than 3 mm above the plate. A coupon's cap measures 4 mm. By how many mm is it too high?
Which document records the actual values used to weld a procedure test plate and the results of its tests?

essays.stem: Explain the steps the Centre would follow to qualify a new GTAW procedure for carbon steel plate, from a draft WPS to an approved one.
essays.modelAnswer: First a draft WPS is written, giving the plate grade and thickness, joint design, position, filler class and size, tungsten type and size, current and polarity, gas and flow rate, and the passes. A skilled welder then welds a test plate to the draft while a witness writes down the real values used: current, voltage, travel speed, gas flow and the number of passes. The coupon is inspected by eye, then cut and tested as the AWS code the Centre uses asks, usually with bend tests and sometimes tensile tests and a macro etch. The real values and the test results are recorded on a PQR, which is signed. If the tests pass, the WPS is finalised from the PQR, with ranges the code allows, and approved for use. If they fail, the cause is found, the draft is changed and a new plate is tested.
markingPoints: Draft WPS lists the main variables (plate, joint, filler, tungsten, current, gas)
Test plate welded with the real values witnessed and recorded
Coupon inspected and tested as the code requires
Results and real values recorded and signed on a PQR
WPS approved from the PQR; failure leads to a change and a retest

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare, fit up and tack a single-V carbon steel plate coupon for an open-root GTAW test in the 3G position.
essays.modelAnswer: I read the WPS for the bevel angle, root face, root gap, filler and current. I check the plates are the grade and thickness on the WPS and mark them with the test number. I bevel each edge, then grind the bevel and the faces on both sides to bright metal, because GTAW has no flux to clean the joint. I file or grind the root face to size and check the angle with a bevel protractor. I wipe the joint with solvent and let it dry. I lay the plates on a flat surface with the root gap set by a spacer and check they line up with no step. I tack at each end with small, fully fused tacks and feather them. I check the gap again, then fix the coupon upright in the stand at the right height. Once fixed, it must not be moved out of position during the test.
markingPoints: Reads the WPS and checks and marks the plates
Bevels and cleans to bright metal on both sides
Sets the root face and checks the angle with a gauge
Sets an even root gap and lines up the plates
Small fused tacks, feathered; coupon fixed in 3G and not moved

essays.stem: Compare GTAW groove welding on plate in the 2G, 3G and 4G positions. Cover the torch angle, where the rod is fed, how the pool is controlled and the faults to watch for.
essays.modelAnswer: In 2G the weld runs level on an upright plate. The torch is held nearly square to the plate, tipped slightly up, and the rod is fed at the upper edge of the pool, because the pool tends to sag onto the lower plate. Overlap at the bottom and undercut at the top are the faults to watch. In 3G the weld runs up the plate. The torch points up at a small angle and the rod is fed into the top of the pool. The welder builds on the shelf of metal below and pauses at the sides so the toes fill, or undercut and a peaked bead follow. In 4G the weld is overhead. The pool must be kept small, with lower current and small dabs of rod, and the arc kept short. Sagging, a concave root and lack of fusion at the toes are the main faults. In every position the welder keeps the arc short and follows the WPS.
markingPoints: 2G: torch tipped up, rod at the upper edge, sag/overlap and undercut
3G: upward, rod into top of pool, pause at sides, undercut risk
4G: small pool, low current, short arc, sag and concave root risk
Names at least one typical fault for each position
Keeps within the WPS in every position

essays.stem: A GTAW plate test has been bent and etched. Explain what each kind of failure in the face bend, the root bend and the macro etch tells you about the welder's technique.
essays.modelAnswer: A face bend puts the cap side in tension. If it opens along the toes or between passes, the welder probably did not fuse the cap or the fill to the side walls, often from too fast a travel or too little heat at the edges. Open pores show gas was lost, from a long arc, draught or dirty metal. A root bend puts the root in tension. A crack along the root edge shows lack of root fusion or penetration, from too small a gap, too thick a root face or too little current. A tungsten inclusion can start a crack too. A macro etch shows the shape of the weld. It can show lack of side-wall fusion, poor penetration, slag-free but cold laps between passes, and the size of each bead. Together, the tests point to what the welder should practise: heat at the side walls, root control or arc length.
markingPoints: Face bend failure: lack of fusion in cap or fill, or porosity, with a cause
Root bend failure: lack of root fusion or penetration, with a cause
Macro etch: shows fusion, penetration and pass shape
Links each result to a technique fault
Uses the results to plan the welder's practice

essays.stem: Explain what a welder's GTAW plate qualification covers, and why a supervisor must check it before giving the welder a job.
essays.modelAnswer: A welder's qualification is recorded on a WPQ. It covers the process (GTAW), and under the AWS code the Centre uses it is limited by the things the welder showed in the test. These include the positions welded, such as 3G and 4G, which may cover other positions too; the range of plate thickness; whether the joint had backing or an open root; the filler group; and the kind of joint, groove or fillet. It also stays in force only while the welder keeps using the process, so the continuity record must be up to date. A supervisor checks the WPQ against the job because a welder who has not shown he can do that position, thickness or open root may make welds that look fine but fail. Using an unqualified welder also breaks the specification, so the client may reject the work.
markingPoints: Names the WPQ and that it is limited to what was tested
Lists at least three limits: position, thickness, backing, filler, joint type
Mentions continuity of use keeping it in force
Explains the risk of hidden faults from an unqualified welder
Explains that the specification and client require it

essays.stem: Describe the hazards of GTAW welding carbon steel, stainless steel and aluminium plate in a test bay, and the controls you would use.
essays.modelAnswer: The arc gives strong ultraviolet light, which burns the eyes and skin. Welders wear a helmet with the right shade, long sleeves and gloves, and screens protect others. Bright aluminium reflects the light, so arms and neck must be covered. Fume is light, but stainless steel fume contains chromium and nickel, so extraction at the bay is used. Argon can collect in pits and low spaces and push out the air, so the bay is ventilated and cylinders are chained upright and turned off after use. The set has high-frequency starting and live parts, so cables and the pedal are checked and kept dry. Tungsten grinding needs a guarded grinder, eye protection and extraction. Hot plates are marked and handled with tongs. Acid etchants and solvents are used with gloves, goggles and the SDS. I follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules.
markingPoints: UV and reflection: shade, cover skin, screens
Fume, especially stainless: extraction
Argon build-up: ventilation and cylinder care
Electrical and HF: checked, dry cables and pedal
Grinding, hot metal and chemicals controlled (SDS, PPE)

essays.stem: Describe how you would GTAW weld and test a fillet weld on carbon steel plate in the 3F position to a WPS.
essays.modelAnswer: I read the WPS for the plate thickness, fillet size, filler, tungsten, current and gas. I clean both plates to bright metal where the weld goes and fit the tee joint tight, with small tacks at the ends. I fix it upright so the weld runs up the joint. I set the current, gas flow and post-flow, and grind the tungsten to a point. I start at the bottom, form a pool that wets both plates, and feed rod into the top edge of the pool, keeping the torch pointing up at a small angle and the arc short. I pause at each toe to stop undercut and keep the leg sizes even. At the end I use the downslope to fill the crater. I check the legs with a fillet gauge and look for undercut and overlap. Then one test piece is broken with the root in tension, and another is cut, polished and etched to show fusion and penetration.
markingPoints: Reads the WPS and cleans and fits up the tee joint
Correct torch angle, rod feed and upward travel
Controls toes and leg size; fills the crater
Checks size and visual faults with a gauge
Fillet break and macro etch tests described

essays.stem: Explain why cleanliness matters so much in GTAW of plate, and describe how you would prepare carbon steel, stainless steel and aluminium plate and their filler rods.
essays.modelAnswer: GTAW has no flux. Anything left on the joint, such as oil, paint, mill scale, rust or oxide, goes into the pool and causes porosity, lack of fusion and a dirty, unstable arc. It can also spoil the tungsten. For carbon steel plate, I grind off mill scale and rust to bright metal on the bevel and both faces, then wipe with solvent. For stainless steel, I use a stainless-only brush and grinding disc so no carbon steel is picked up, and wipe with solvent. For aluminium, I remove oil with solvent first, then brush the oxide off with a stainless brush kept only for aluminium, and weld soon after, because the oxide grows back. Filler rods are kept in their sealed, labelled tubes, handled with clean gloves, wiped before use if dusty, and the dirty end is cut off. Solvent must be dry before the arc is struck.
markingPoints: Explains why: no flux, so dirt gives porosity and poor fusion
Carbon steel: grind to bright metal and degrease
Stainless: separate tools, no carbon steel pick-up
Aluminium: degrease, then remove oxide and weld soon
Filler rods kept clean and labelled; solvent dry first

essays.stem: You are running a GTAW plate qualification test for five trainees. Explain how you would plan and control the test so the results are fair and can be trusted.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the day, I check the WPS, gather plates of the right grade and thickness, and make sure each bay has a working set, argon, the right filler and tungsten. I mark each coupon with a number and the welder's name, so coupons cannot be swapped. I brief the trainees on the WPS, the test rules and safety. I witness fit-up and check that each coupon is fixed in its stated position and stays there. I watch the welding, record the settings and note anything outside the WPS. Each trainee welds only his own coupon. After welding, I inspect each coupon by eye and record the results before any are cut. Bend strips are cut from the places the code sets, labelled, and bent in front of a witness. I record every result, pass or fail, on the WPQ forms and keep the strips until the records are signed.
markingPoints: Prepares WPS, plates, sets and consumables before the test
Marks coupons so they are traced to each welder
Witnesses fit-up, position and settings during welding
Inspects, cuts and tests coupons as the code sets
Records all results on WPQ forms and keeps evidence

essays.stem: Explain the causes of tungsten inclusions and arc strikes on GTAW plate welds, how each is found, and how a welder prevents them.
essays.modelAnswer: A tungsten inclusion is a piece of tungsten left in the weld. It happens when the tungsten touches the pool or the rod, when it is scratch started, when the current is too high for the tungsten size so the tip melts, or when the tip cracks. It is found by radiography, where it shows as a bright spot, or it may start a crack in a bend test. To prevent it, the welder uses high-frequency or lift-arc starting, chooses the right tungsten size, keeps a steady short arc, and stops to regrind the tungsten and grind out the spot if it is dipped. An arc strike is a mark where the arc touched the plate outside the joint. It is found by eye. It can leave a hard spot or a tiny crack. To prevent it, the welder starts the arc in the joint or on a start tab and keeps the torch and cables tidy.
markingPoints: Gives at least two causes of tungsten inclusions
Says how tungsten inclusions are found (radiography or bend)
Gives prevention for tungsten inclusions
Explains arc strikes, why they matter and how found
Gives prevention for arc strikes

practical1.title: GTAW open-root groove test coupons in carbon steel plate in the 3G and 4G positions, with bend tests and WPQ records
practical1.brief: Your group is given a WPS for a single-V groove weld in carbon steel plate with an open root, welded with GTAW. The assessor tells each member to weld either a 3G (vertical) or a 4G (overhead) coupon, so both positions are covered in the group. Each member checks the plates, bevels and cleans them, sets the root face and gap, tacks, and fixes the coupon in position at the stand. Each member then welds the root, fill and cap with GTAW to the WPS, without moving the coupon. One member acts as witness for each welder in turn, writing the real current, gas flow and tungsten on the group's record sheet. When the coupons are cool, each member inspects another member's coupon by eye and records the result. The assessor chooses two coupons for face and root bend tests; the group marks out and grinds the strips. Each member fills in a draft WPQ for his or her own test. Photograph each stage below.
materials: Carbon steel plate, about 6 mm thick, cut for one coupon per member (about 150 mm × 125 mm pieces, or as the assessor sets)
ER70S-2 filler rods, 1.6 mm and 2.4 mm, in labelled tubes
GTAW sets on DCEN with lift-arc or HF start, torches, cups and 2.4 mm tungstens
Argon cylinders with regulators and flowmeters
Welding stands that hold coupons in 3G and 4G
Grinder, files, bevel protractor, weld gauge, solvent and clean rags
WPS, witness record sheet and blank WPQ forms (from the assessor)
Saw and guided bend jig (used by the assessor or under direct supervision)
photos: A fitted and tacked coupon with the root gap gauge in place
Each coupon fixed in its stand in 3G or 4G before welding
A root pass seen from the back of the coupon
Finished caps on every member's coupon, with the coupon numbers showing
Bend strips after bending, labelled face and root
checklist: Checked and cleaned the plates to bright metal and set root face and gap to the WPS
Fixed the coupon in the stated position and did not move it during the test
Set current, gas flow and tungsten to the WPS
Welded a fully fused root with even penetration and no tungsten inclusions
Laid fill and cap passes with no undercut, overlap or arc strikes
Witnessed another member's test and recorded real values correctly
Inspected a coupon by eye and recorded the result correctly
Completed a draft WPQ for his or her own test
safety: Weld only in screened bays with extraction on; wear a helmet with the right shade, gloves and long sleeves
Chain argon cylinders upright and close them after use; keep the bay ventilated
Grind tungstens only on the guarded grinder with eye protection
Handle hot coupons with tongs and mark them HOT
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: GTAW fillet welds on carbon steel plate in the 3F and 4F positions, with fillet break and macro etch tests and a PQR-style record
practical2.brief: Your group is to show that a GTAW fillet procedure on carbon steel plate works in the vertical (3F) and overhead (4F) positions. Using the draft WPS from the assessor, each member fits up and welds two tee joints: one in 3F and one in 4F, single pass, to the fillet size given. One member records the real values used for each weld (current, gas flow, tungsten, filler, time) on the group's PQR-style sheet. Each member checks his or her own fillets with a fillet gauge and records the leg sizes. The group then breaks one tee joint per member with the root in tension, and cuts, grinds and etches one cross-section from the 3F and one from the 4F joint, under supervision. The group writes up the results and says whether the draft WPS should be approved, changed or re-tested. Photograph each stage below.
materials: Carbon steel plate, about 6 mm thick, cut for two tee joints per member
ER70S-2 filler rods in labelled tubes
GTAW sets on DCEN, torches, tungstens and argon with flowmeters
Stands to hold work in 3F and 4F
Fillet weld gauge, grinder, files, solvent and rags
Press, vice or hammer set-up for fillet break tests
Saw, fine abrasive papers and etching solution with its SDS (used under supervision)
Draft WPS and blank PQR-style record sheet (from the assessor)

checklist: Cleaned and fitted the tee joints tightly with small, fused tacks
Welded the 3F fillet upward with even legs and no undercut
Welded the 4F fillet with a controlled pool and no sagging
Measured the leg sizes correctly and recorded them
Took part in the break and etch tests safely and read the results correctly
Recorded real values and helped reach a sound decision on the WPS
safety: Wear goggles, gloves and an apron when using the etching solution; read its SDS and work with ventilation
Stand clear of the break test and use a guard or cover
Wear full welding PPE; extra care with neck and arm cover when welding overhead
Follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules
